short: The fast tank built to exploit the breach the heavies made, and to replace cavalry.
full:
William Tritton designed the Medium Mark A privately at Foster's as a machine to do what heavy tanks could not: move at the speed of events. Its prototype ran on 3 February 1917. Two 45 hp Tylor lorry engines drove one track each, giving 8 mph, and a crew of three fought four Hotchkiss machine guns from a fixed rear barbette. Steering by matching engine speeds was awkward enough that drivers could stall one side and spin the tank. Two hundred were built.

Twelve went into action on 26 March 1918 near Hébuterne, catching German infantry advancing in the open during the spring offensive and running for sixteen hours without a breakdown. At Amiens on 8 August, ninety-six Whippets worked with the Cavalry Corps; one, Musical Box, spent nine hours alone behind German lines shooting up transport, an observation balloon and an artillery battery before it was set alight. Whippets later served in the Russian Civil War, in Ireland and in Japan, some into the 1930s.
